parts.note: Labour is the party of the political left

explanation.surface: A rift opens between Britain's two main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a crack or division, so it is a synonym of split as a noun.

parts.note: a heraldic emblem described as if it were a garment worn over a soldier's weapons, its literal name

explanation.definitionFit: A family's heraldic emblem; literally a tunic worn over armour bore the design in battle.

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
a plant is something that grows

explanation.surface: Advice to promote the growing of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is a playful one tied to the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the purple vegetable the British call aubergine.

clue.text: Not a very bright lot, but sturdy

parts.note: thick is slang for stupid, not very bright
a set is a group or lot

explanation.surface: A dim-witted group who are at least strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means heavily built and stocky, a synonym of sturdy.

clue.text: In the midst of drama, detectives left calmly

indicators.note: placing one thing in the midst of another signals an insertion here

parts.note: a play is a drama
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police officers walk off a theatre set without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe acting in a quiet, serene, unruffled manner.

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: keep means support or maintain, as in keep a family

explanation.surface: Searching for a means of upward support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns KEEP upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick look or glance.

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the word for carriage

parts.note: a coupe is a type of closed carriage or car

explanation.surface: Something left behind in a horse-drawn carriage and its pair of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside COUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is two of something, the same as a pair.

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the day are jumbled

explanation.surface: A power source takes the start of the week as holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator that supplies electric current.

explanation.surface: A place versus a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of York was a royal dynasty in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: York is an English city, and the House of York was a royal family line.

clue.text: In time a possible giver of pain

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes in the word for time, so this signals an insertion

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: a possible version of the word is one of its rearrangements

explanation.surface: Someone who may eventually cause hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a possible giver of pain' reads as one phrase, but 'possible' is the signal on giver and 'pain' alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pain someone, as a verb, is to distress or wrong them, which is to aggrieve them.

parts.note: to knap is to chip flint into shape
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: Choosing between a crisp packet and some other receptacle.
explanation.walkthrough: Knapping is the old craft of chipping flint into tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, so it is a kind of container.

parts.note: grand seems to mean splendid, but it is the first word of a famous horse race run on a racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired with the first word, this makes the name of the famous British steeplechase, a great sporting occasion on a racecourse.

clue.text: Use suntan lotion, it helps in the rain

explanation.surface: Sunshine protection set against rain protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: to put oil on your skin, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof coat of oiled cloth, worn in wet weather; the first reading splits it as oil plus skin.

clue.text: Points me out as example of relative favouritism

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone singles me out as an instance of favouring family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POINTS ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially in giving jobs.

parts.note: a French phrase meaning just between ourselves, in confidence, rather than a soldier of France

explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means confidentially, in private between the speakers.

parts.note: Uncle Sam stands for the United States; the American word for the straps holding up trousers

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain braces hold up trousers and suspenders hold up stockings; Americans use the latter word for braces.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English this is the word for the straps over the shoulders that hold up trousers.

clue.text: Revolutionary system to increase the harvest

definitions.text: Revolutionary system to increase the harvest

parts.words: Revolutionary system to increase the harvest
parts.note: revolutionary suggests political upheaval, but here it means taking turns in a cycle, as farmers vary what each field grows year by year

explanation.definitionFit: The farming practice of changing the plants grown in each field in a cycle keeps soil fertile and raises yields.

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Choosing between a cooking pot, a tin and a cracked bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges BASIN to NABIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for the drug cannabis.

clue.text: It's to do with the pursuit of game, naturally

definitions.text: It's to do with the pursuit of game

explanation.surface: Hunting described as natural.
explanation.walkthrough: Coursing is the hunting of hares with dogs, so something of coursing concerns the pursuit of game.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course means naturally or certainly; read cryptically it means relating to coursing, chasing game.

clue.text: A foreign girl who drops in after marriage

definitions.text: A foreign girl who drops in after marriage

parts.words: A foreign girl who drops in after marriage
parts.note: an Italian young unmarried woman; after marriage her title loses the letters I and N, becoming the title for a married lady

explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like visiting, but it means dropping the letters IN: Italian for Miss becomes Signora, Mrs, once married.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian title and word for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Capacity to get on after bitterness?

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: gall means bitterness or resentment

explanation.surface: Wondering whether resentment helps someone get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of capacity or volume.

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a lid on a box
a rush is a tall grass-like plant growing in wet places

explanation.surface: Animals charge across tall grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a forceful forward surge, like a stampede.

parts.note: the bright green cloth worn by Robin Hood's outlaws is named after an English cathedral city and county town

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is traditionally dressed in Lincoln green, a cloth once made in Lincoln, county town of Lincolnshire in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is the traditional colour of Robin Hood's band, named after the English city where the dyed cloth was made.

indicators.note: one word is found surrounding another, so this is a container signal

parts.note: drums are barrel-shaped containers
ancient means old

explanation.surface: Old casks discovered at a historic rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumps' looks like rubbish tips, but here it is the low mood of being down in the dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps and being in the doldrums both mean feeling gloomy and low.

clue.text: Spot the sign of a faulty washer

definitions.text: the sign of a faulty washer

explanation.surface: Noticing a leaking tap's telltale sign.
explanation.walkthrough: A worn washer in a tap lets water leak drop by drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a drop or spot of liquid, and a dripping tap shows a worn washer.

explanation.surface: A flavouring compared with a child of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt is an old word for a sailor, playfully a son of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt food is to season it, and an old salt is an experienced sailor.

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
borne is a past participle of bear, meaning carried

explanation.surface: A melody drifts up into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried in the air is up high, flying or floating.

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a song, sung or intoned

explanation.surface: Someone with a fondness for songwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or tendency, a synonym of inclination.

explanation.surface: Talented performers also commit blunders.
